operator_io_quirks: No PRIMARY KEY declared on ANY table (pk=[] everywhere); sample_fresh_primary_keys/drop_unique_duplicates are no-ops here, so TS row counts survive unfiltered.

fielding_postseason has a dangling FK: team_id -> player(team_id) (parent col exists but is not a key of player); parent_exists=true so it is NOT dropped, and FK filling will draw player.team_id values (which don't exist) into fielding_postseason.team_id.

Many NUMERIC columns store mixed storage classes: integer, real AND text (e.g. pitching.baopp/era, team.fp is real-only, player_award_vote.points_won integer+real). Empty-string '' appears as a value in NUMERIC columns (gp, gs, g_dh, ibb, hbp, sh, sf, g_idp, death_*, ballots, needed, attendance, dp, cs, hbp, sf).
Empty string '' is a real value in many TEXT columns (league_id, div_id, tie, notes, park_alias, bats, throws, death_*, inducted-adjacent, active, na_assoc, div_win/wc_win/lg_win/ws_win).
Text-stored dates: player.debut, player.final_game, home_game.span_first, home_game.span_last are TEXT with format YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. '2004-04-06'); declared TEXT so TS dispatches String, not Date.
player_id is TEXT and is the de-facto key of player (distinct=18846=rows) but has no PK/unique constraint; child FKs to player.player_id are non-unique-parent-safe only because values are distinct.
team.team_id is TEXT, distinct=149 over 2805 rows (non-unique parent: same team_id across years); FK children (appearances, batting, home_game, manager, etc.) reference a NON-UNIQUE parent column.
Large tables: fielding 170526, batting 101332, appearances 100951, pitching 44139, salary 25575 — all under 300000 so full read is fine, but read once per worker.
Column named 'double' (batting, batting_postseason, team) and 'rank', 'year', 'round', 'a', 'e', 'r', 'h', 'w', 'l', 'g' — short/reserved-ish names; must be double-quoted in generated SQL.
pitching_postseason.baopp is TEXT (not NUMERIC like pitching.baopp) — same logical column, different declared type across tables.
manager_award.notes is NUMERIC but only value is '' (distinct=1); player_award.notes is TEXT with 29 distinct values — same name, different type.
No views/triggers/indexes mentioned in DDL; all tables plain CREATE TABLE with inline FK clauses (no named constraints).
operator_ts_expectations: All TEXT columns -> String fuzzer: random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() with contamination; player_id/team_id/college_id/park_id get implausible random strings, breaking joins to real-looking ids -> likely FN on queries filtering by specific id patterns.

All INTEGER columns -> Number fuzzer (is_int, scale 0): values in [-1,1] perturbed by +-1/+-2; year columns get tiny values (0,1,-1) instead of 1871-2015 -> FN for year-range predicates, FP for year=0/1 ties.
All NUMERIC columns -> Number fuzzer scale 0 (no args): same tiny integer range; era/fp/baopp (real-valued) get integers 0/1/-1 -> FN for era<3.0 style predicates, FP from mass ties at 0/1.
String fuzzer on league_id/div_id/tie/inducted/bats/throws produces random strings, not the small enum sets (AL/NL, Y/N, R/L) -> FN for league_id='NL' predicates, FP from random collisions.
Text-stored dates (debut, span_first/last) get String fuzzer random strings, not YYYY-MM-DD -> FN for date-range/format predicates; no Date fuzzer fires on this DB.

FK filling: child player_id/team_id/park_id/college_id drawn with replacement from parent's generated values; parent player has 18846 distinct random strings so child gets plausible-looking-but-random ids -> joins mostly match (good for join queries) but values implausible.
fielding_postseason.team_id filled from player.team_id (dangling FK) -> values are player_id-like strings, never match team.team_id -> FN on fielding_postseason JOIN team.
No PK/unique constraints -> no row dropping; TS keeps all generated rows, so duplicate-heavy tables (year, league_id) get many ties -> FP for DISTINCT/COUNT(DISTINCT) and GROUP BY queries.
Empty-string values in original are sampled as elements (5 originals + pool) so '' survives in league_id/div_id/tie -> some queries filtering league_id='' may still match.
Number fuzzer list-range quirk (upper end overwritten to full range) means even with original elements, fresh draws dominate -> implausible magnitudes.
String fuzzer adds str(i+1)/str(i-1) for int-like strings and %-stripped variants -> some numeric-looking text (baopp '0.23') gets near-miss variants.
